question: Should ClawRouter support a second production deployment target outside Cloudflare, and what minimum security, durability, and operational parity must that target guarantee?
rationale: Cloudflare primitives currently form authoritative production infrastructure, so Docker support changes product scope, trust boundaries, persistence guarantees, and long-term support obligations rather than merely adding packaging.

options.title: Sponsor portable production runtime
options.body: Define a runtime-neutral contract and require Docker parity for revocation, budgets, identity, retention, migrations, queues, audit, backup, and upgrades.

options.title: Keep Cloudflare production-only
options.body: Document Wrangler as development-only and continue requiring Cloudflare-managed primitives for supported production deployments.

options.title: Offer evaluation container
options.body: Provide a best-effort local container without promising production durability, security, migration, or operational parity.

recommendation.title: Sponsor portable production runtime
recommendation.body: Define a runtime-neutral contract and require Docker parity for revocation, budgets, identity, retention, migrations, queues, audit, backup, and upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The most recent central data-plane, authority, storage, and deployment history follows from the TypeScript runtime refactor and subsequent Cloudflare-focused work.
